high.title: Ringgit closes flat as FOMC minutes weigh on US dollar
high.summary: The ringgit held steady as FOMC minutes signaled the Fed may keep rates unchanged for the rest of the year, while Bank Negara Malaysia maintained the OPR at 2.75% for the seventh consecutive period. The stable OPR stance is seen as ringgit-positive, reinforcing expectations of monetary policy stability throughout 2026. Malaysia's GDP growth projection of 4%-5% for 2026 remains on track, providing confidence in the domestic economic outlook.

high.title: Bursa closes lower amid renewed geopolitical tensions
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia closed lower as US military strikes on Iranian targets raised concerns over global energy supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz, dampening investor sentiment. Despite the weaker index, market breadth improved with gainers leading across key sectors, suggesting selective bargain hunting. BNM's decision to hold the OPR at 2.75% provided policy certainty and underpinned confidence in the domestic economic outlook.

high.title: Bursa gives up gains on renewed Middle East uncertainty
high.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped in early trade after Trump announced the end of a ceasefire agreement with Iran, reigniting Middle East tensions and causing caution on Wall Street overnight. Investor sentiment was rattled by escalating geopolitical risks that could affect global energy markets and supply chains. Malaysian equities faced selling pressure despite positive market breadth, with turnover remaining modest.

high.title: BNM May Hold Policy Rate, Signal Upcoming Hike as AI Boosts Economic Growth
high.summary: Bank Negara Malaysia is widely expected to hold its overnight policy rate at 2.75% at its 3pm decision, with 24 out of 25 economists surveyed by Bloomberg forecasting no change. The decision comes amid regional rate hikes driven by the Iran war and currency pressures, while Malaysia benefits from AI-driven export demand and local fuel subsidies. Any signal of a future rate hike would be significant for bond and equity markets.

high.title: Ringgit Rises as Fed Minutes Weigh on US Dollar
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0730/4.0800 against the US dollar after FOMC minutes revealed Fed officials are divided between holding or raising rates, with no further cuts being considered. The current federal funds rate stands at 3.50%-3.75%, and the hawkish tilt is weighing on the US Dollar Index. This shift in US monetary policy outlook has direct implications for ringgit valuation and Malaysian capital flows.

high.title: Ringgit eases against US dollar as Middle East tensions rise
high.summary: The ringgit weakened to 4.0745/4.0830 against the US dollar following US military strikes against Iranian forces and revocation of a waiver on Iranian oil sales. Brent crude prices surged 6.13% to US$76.40 per barrel, signalling heightened geopolitical risk. Malaysian investors should monitor risk-off sentiment and rising energy costs that could impact import-dependent sectors.

high.title: Ringgit ends higher as weaker greenback, firmer oil lift sentiment
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0685/4.0735 against the US dollar, supported by a softer US ISM services PMI reading and technical oversold conditions. Markets are now awaiting the FOMC meeting minutes for clearer signals on the Fed's interest rate trajectory. This has direct implications for Malaysian currency positioning and capital flow dynamics.

high.title: Ringgit may rebound on capital flow measures, say analysts
high.summary: Analysts from RBC and ANZ forecast significant ringgit strengthening, with targets of RM3.95 and RM3.80 per dollar respectively by year-end. BNM's intensified measures to encourage repatriation and conversion of overseas earnings, combined with a solid trade surplus and foreign bond inflows, are driving optimism. This echoes successful 2024 interventions that made the ringgit Asia's strongest currency that year.

high.title: Ringgit opens firmer as traders reassess US rate hike prospects
high.summary: The ringgit opened stable at 4.0695/4.0780 against the USD as the Fed chair's reluctance to provide forward rate guidance reduced hike expectations. Two key events on Thursday, July 9 — FOMC minutes release and BNM's MPC meeting — are set to be major market catalysts. Investors and businesses should closely monitor these events for signals on interest rate direction in both the US and Malaysia.

medium.title: Palantir says UK police contract wrongly blocked over values and ethics
medium.summary: Palantir is challenging a London High Court ruling after the Mayor's office blocked a £50 million AI contract with the Metropolitan Police, citing concerns about the company's values and failure to hold an open competition. The case highlights growing European scrutiny over dependency on US tech platforms, particularly those with military and immigration ties. This is relevant to Malaysian investors and policymakers as Malaysia actively courts US tech firms for AI and digital infrastructure partnerships.

medium.title: UST partners with Anthropic to help Global 1000 firms become AI-native
medium.summary: UST has partnered with Anthropic to embed Claude AI into enterprise workflows for the world's 1,000 largest publicly traded companies across healthcare, telecommunications, and banking sectors. The partnership involves deploying up to 20,000 AI-focused associates to guide digital transformation. This is relevant to Malaysian businesses and banks as AI-native adoption accelerates globally, signaling rising competitive pressure and transformation opportunities in key domestic sectors.

medium.title: Bursa Ends Higher on Late Buying Interest
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI edged up 0.68 points to close at 1,683.61 despite pressure from rising crude oil prices following US airstrikes on Iranian targets and the revocation of Iran's oil export waiver. Late institutional buying provided support, signalling resilient domestic sentiment amid geopolitical uncertainty. Investors are monitoring energy price impacts on inflation and the global interest rate outlook.

medium.title: Bursa Opens Higher, Outperforms Regional Peers
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 6.42 points at open to 1,689.35, outperforming regional peers despite a Wall Street sell-off driven by AI stock weakness and Strait of Hormuz tensions pushing Brent crude to around US$74 per barrel. Hong Kong's Hang Seng slipped below 23,500 amid renewed AI-related selling, while US 10-year Treasury yields edged higher. Malaysia's relative resilience stands out against a broadly risk-off regional backdrop.

medium.title: Ringgit Ends Higher Against Major Currencies but Slips Versus US Dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit slipped against the US dollar as crude oil prices surged 5.68% to US$78.28 per barrel following US military strikes on Iranian forces and the revocation of Iran's oil export waiver. Concerns over potential closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global oil shipping route, heightened market anxiety. Upcoming FOMC minutes were flagged as a key watch item for further currency direction.

medium.title: Bursa ends marginally lower on mild profit-taking
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI eased slightly by 0.60 points to 1,682.93, reflecting cautious sentiment and normal consolidation after recent gains. Analysts note the index remains above recent lows, suggesting the short-term recovery is intact. Easing geopolitical tensions and moderating energy prices are expected to provide continued market support.

medium.title: Bursa slips after recent gains as sellers return
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped 4.01 points or 0.24% to 1,679.52 in early trade as sellers returned following recent gains, with market breadth slightly negative. Turnover was modest at 163.91 million shares worth RM54.48 million, reflecting cautious investor sentiment. This signals short-term consolidation pressure for equity market participants.

medium.title: Ringgit opens slightly higher amid focus on Fed outlook
medium.summary: The ringgit opened marginally higher at 4.0815/4.0880 against the US dollar, though it weakened against most major currencies. Fed Governor Waller's hawkish stance on maintaining the 2% inflation target reinforces a higher-for-longer interest rate environment, keeping the US dollar well supported. Malaysian businesses with USD exposure should factor in continued currency headwinds.

medium.title: Bursa ends higher, lifted by banking and plantation stocks
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI closed up 4.48 points at 1,683.53, driven by easing geopolitical tensions and declining crude oil prices supporting blue-chip stocks. Despite the index gain, market breadth remained negative with losers outpacing gainers 620 to 403. Bargain-hunting in fundamentally sound stocks suggests cautious but improving domestic investor sentiment.

medium.title: Ringgit slips as investors return to US dollar after weak jobs report
medium.summary: The ringgit eased to 4.0825/4.0875 against the USD by 6pm, as investors shifted back to the dollar despite weak US jobs data. Caution ahead of the FOMC minutes release and the US ISM services index publication added to pressure on Asian currencies broadly. Bank Muamalat's chief economist flagged the ISM consensus estimate of 54.2 for June as a key data point to watch.

medium.title: Bursa opens firmer on improved investor sentiment
medium.summary: Bursa opened firmer with the FBM KLCI rising 1.13 points to 1,680.18, buoyed by Wall Street's positive close and diminishing US rate hike expectations following weak May jobs data. Rakuten Trade's Kenny Yee projected the index to trade in the 1,675–1,695 range, suggesting limited near-term volatility. Easing rate hike concerns could encourage equity inflows into the Malaysian market.
